functions.name: tcmalloc::malloc_tracing_extension::GetAllocatedAddressRanges
functions.description: Returns a snapshot of the address ranges currently owned by TCMalloc at the granularity of allocator Spans. No arguments are required; there are no documented preconditions on process state or thread context.
Do not assume that every object within a returned size-class span is currently allocated; only that the span is owned by TCMalloc.
Interpret SpanDetails::object_size as the size-class bytes for size-class spans and as 0 for large, non–size-class objects.

functions.name: MallocTracingExtension_Internal_GetAllocatedAddressRanges

Expected usage: call with no arguments to query current allocated address ranges, then check status.ok() and, if OK, consume the AllocatedAddressRanges result. Notes: This symbol is only declared when ABSL_HAVE_ATTRIBUTE_WEAK is true and not on Apple or Emscripten platforms. Any specifics of AllocatedAddressRanges (structure, ordering, or units) are defined in tcmalloc::malloc_tracing_extension; details beyond that are unknown from this header.
requirements: This function is only declared when ABSL_HAVE_ATTRIBUTE_WEAK is true and the target platform is not Apple and not Emscripten; otherwise it is unavailable at compile time.
Callers must check the absl::StatusOr status (status().ok() or ok()) before accessing the contained AllocatedAddressRanges value.
Consumers must include and link against Abseil StatusOr and TCMalloc tracing extension definitions so that absl::StatusOr and tcmalloc::malloc_tracing_extension::AllocatedAddressRanges are available.
Behavior and contents of AllocatedAddressRanges are defined externally; do not assume ordering, uniqueness, or units without consulting tcmalloc/malloc_tracing_extension.h.
Thread-safety, blocking behavior, and performance characteristics are unknown from this header; callers should not assume thread-safety without external documentation.

functions.name: alloc_at_least
functions.description: Allocates at least min_size bytes and returns both the allocated pointer and the actual allocation size in an alloc_result_t. Intended for callers that can benefit from using more than the minimum (e.g., growth strategies) and want to avoid a second size query. On allocation failure, typical behavior (inferred from malloc-like APIs) is that ptr is NULL and size is 0. The allocation is suitable for general-purpose use; details such as exact alignment and failure semantics are not documented here and are inferred from common allocator conventions.
requirements: min_size specifies the minimum number of bytes requested; the allocator may return result.size >= min_size (inferred).
Caller must check result.ptr before use; if result.ptr is NULL, treat the allocation as failed and do not dereference it (inferred from malloc-like behavior).
Caller must only read/write within [result.ptr, result.ptr + result.size) and must not assume result.size == min_size (inferred).

The returned pointer should be released using the allocator’s compatible deallocation routine (e.g., free) when no longer needed; mixing allocators is not allowed (inferred; exact deallocator is not specified in this header).
No guarantee is stated about thread-safety, errno, or out-of-memory signaling beyond the return value; such behavior is unknown.

functions.description: Allocates at least min_size bytes with the returned pointer aligned to alignment, returning both the pointer and the actual allocated size in an alloc_result_t. Useful when an alignment constraint must be met while still allowing the allocator to provide more than the minimum. On failure, typical behavior (inferred from aligned_alloc/posix_memalign patterns) is that ptr is NULL and size is 0. Exact constraints on alignment are not documented here; common conventions are stated as inferred requirements.
requirements: alignment must be a non-zero power of two (inferred from aligned_alloc/posix_memalign conventions).
alignment should be a multiple of sizeof(void*) and at least alignof(max_align_t) for general-purpose objects (inferred).
min_size specifies the minimum number of bytes requested; the allocator may return result.size >= min_size (inferred).
Caller must check result.ptr before use; if result.ptr is NULL, treat as allocation failure and do not dereference (inferred).
Caller must only access memory within [result.ptr, result.ptr + result.size) and must not assume result.size == min_size (inferred).

The returned pointer should be freed using the allocator’s compatible deallocation routine (e.g., free) when no longer needed; do not mix with a different allocator (inferred; exact deallocator is not specified in this header).
If alignment requirements are violated, behavior is unknown; caller must supply a valid alignment as above (inferred).

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for:
# - MallocExtension_Internal_GetNumericProperty(name_data, name_size, &value)
# - tcmalloc::tcmalloc_internal::AbslParseFlag(text, preference, ...)
# Both consume arbitrary byte strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
#
# Strategy:
# - Emphasize realistic property names that the allocator may recognize, to
#   drive code paths returning true and writing a value.
# - Mix in edge-case byte buffers (empty, very long, with NULs, non-ASCII, and
#   names that are off-by-one from real names) to exercise negative paths.
# - For AbslParseFlag, include valid tokens and nearby invalid variations.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Return a single bytes buffer; fuzz harness will slice it as needed for
#   FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls.

# A curated list of commonly exposed TCMalloc property names (subset gleaned
# from public docs and typical deployments). Even if a particular build does not
# support some, they remain reasonable candidates.
KNOWN_PROPERTIES: List[bytes] = [
    b"generic.current_allocated_bytes",
    b"generic.heap_size",
    b"generic.metadata_allocated",
    b"tcmalloc.page_heap_free_bytes",
    b"tcmalloc.page_heap_unmapped_bytes",
    b"tcmalloc.slack_bytes",
    b"tcmalloc.thread_cache_bytes",
    b"tcmalloc.central_cache_free_bytes",
    b"tcmalloc.transfer_cache_free_bytes",
    b"tcmalloc.max_total_thread_cache_bytes",
    b"tcmalloc.current_total_thread_cache_bytes",
    b"tcmalloc.max_per_cpu_cache_size",
    b"tcmalloc.per_cpu_caches_active",
    b"tcmalloc.background_release_rate_bytes_per_second",
]

# Valid tokens for AbslParseFlag(MadvisePreference)
VALID_TOKENS = [b"NEVER", b"DONTNEED", b"FREE_AND_DONTNEED", b"FREE_ONLY"]

# Nearby-invalid variants to ensure parse failures
INVALID_NEAR = [
    b"never", b"DontNeed", b"FREE-AND-DONTNEED", b"FREEONLY",
    b"NEVER\x00TRAIL", b" DONTNEED", b"FREE_AND_DONTNEED ", b"FREE_ONLY!",
]


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._:/-"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n)).encode('ascii')


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _with_nuls(rng: random.Random, base: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not base:
        return b"\x00"
    b = bytearray(base)
    # Insert a few NULs at random positions
    for _ in range(1 + rng.randrange(3)):
        pos = rng.randrange(len(b) + 1)
        b.insert(pos, 0)
    return bytes(b)


def _perturb(rng: random.Random, s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Small random edits (insert, delete, substitute) to make near-miss names
    b = bytearray(s)
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(1, 4)):
        op = rng.randrange(3)
        if op == 0 and b:  # substitute
            i = rng.randrange(len(b))
            b[i] = rng.randrange(256)
        elif op == 1 and b:  # delete
            del b[rng.randrange(len(b))]
        else:  # insert
            i = rng.randrange(len(b)+1)
            b.insert(i, rng.randrange(256))
    return bytes(b)


def _make_property_name(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.45:
        # Likely-valid name
        s = rng.choice(KNOWN_PROPERTIES)
        # Occasionally add valid prefixes/suffixes that some impls accept
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            s = b"/" + s
        return s
    elif choice < 0.7:
        # Near-miss property
        base = rng.choice(KNOWN_PROPERTIES)
        return _perturb(rng, base)
    elif choice < 0.85:
        # Random ASCII-ish name
        return _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 64))
    else:
        # Random bytes, possibly with NULs
        raw = _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            raw = _with_nuls(rng, raw)
        return raw


def _make_flag_text(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    r = rng.random()
    if r < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(VALID_TOKENS)
    elif r < 0.75:
        return rng.choice(INVALID_NEAR)
    elif r < 0.9:
        # Random ASCII token
        return _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, 24))
    else:
        # Random bytes including possible NULs
        return _with_nuls(rng, _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 24)))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Compose several entries; the harness may request multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
    # values in sequence. We'll pack them as length-prefixed to allow the
    # harness (or splitting logic) to separate, but even if it doesn't, each
    # is valid standalone text or binary substring.
    # Format: [count][len][blob]... where count/len are 2-byte little-endian.
    # If the harness ignores framing and reads raw bytes, it still gets a rich
    # mix of tokens and property names, starting with a plausible ASCII one.

    entries: List[bytes] = []

    # Ensure at least one valid property and one valid flag token appear early
    entries.append(rng.choice(KNOWN_PROPERTIES))
    entries.append(rng.choice(VALID_TOKENS))

    # Add a mix of additional property-like names and flags
    total_target = rng.randint(6, 16)
    for _ in range(total_target):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            entries.append(_make_property_name(rng))
        else:
            entries.append(_make_flag_text(rng))

    # Add some edge cases
    edge_cases = [
        b"",                      # empty
        b"\x00",                  # single NUL
        b"DONTNEED\x00NEVER",     # valid token with embedded NUL
        _with_nuls(rng, rng.choice(KNOWN_PROPERTIES)),
        _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(65, 256)),  # longer random blob
    ]
    entries.extend(edge_cases)

    # Serialize with simple 2-byte LE lengths to keep under 4096 bytes
    def pack_le16(n: int) -> bytes:
        return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF))

    blob = bytearray()
    blob += pack_le16(len(entries))
    for e in entries:
        e = e[:1024]  # cap individual entry length
        blob += pack_le16(len(e))
        blob += e
        if len(blob) > 4000:
            break

    # Ensure final size <= 4096
    return bytes(blob[:4096])

import random
from typing import List

# Target format: fixed token string for tcmalloc::tcmalloc_internal::AbslParseFlag
# Accepted tokens: "NEVER", "DONTNEED", "FREE_AND_DONTNEED", "FREE_ONLY"
# Fuzzer stub sometimes takes FUZZ_PARAM_STR() from the provided buffer. We
# therefore emit one token per buffer, optionally surrounded by common
# whitespace or newline patterns to exercise absl::string_view handling paths
# that callers might try (even though the implementation expects exact tokens).
# We also occasionally emit clearly invalid strings to drive the failure path.

VALID_TOKENS: List[str] = [
    "NEVER",
    "DONTNEED",
    "FREE_AND_DONTNEED",
    "FREE_ONLY",
]

INVALID_EXAMPLES: List[str] = [
    "never",               # case mismatch
    "DONT_NEED",           # underscore variant
    "FREE-AND-DONTNEED",   # punctuation
    "FREE ONLY",           # space
    "",                    # empty
    "UNKNOWN",
    "123",
    "DON'TNEED",           # apostrophe
    "FREE_AND_DONT_NEED",
]

SURROUNDS = [
    ("", ""),
    ("\n", "\n"),
    (" ", ""),
    ("\t", "\t"),
    ("\r\n", "\r\n"),
]

TRAILERS = [
    "", "\n", "\0", " #comment", "\t#cmt\n"
]

def _pick_weighted(rng: random.Random, items, weights):
    total = sum(weights)
    x = rng.uniform(0, total)
    acc = 0.0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if x <= acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose whether to generate a valid or invalid token.
    # Favor valid tokens to exercise success path more often, but keep
    # a good portion invalid for the failure path in the stub.
    generate_valid = _pick_weighted(rng, [True, False], [0.7, 0.3])

    if generate_valid:
        token = rng.choice(VALID_TOKENS)
        # Occasionally add benign surrounds that some parsers tolerate; the
        # current implementation requires exact match, but the stub mixes in
        # arbitrary strings elsewhere. We primarily keep exact tokens.
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            pre, suf = rng.choice(SURROUNDS)
            s = f"{pre}{token}{suf}"
        else:
            s = token
        # Rarely add a trailing newline or NUL to simulate common input sources.
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            s += rng.choice(TRAILERS)
    else:
        base = rng.choice(INVALID_EXAMPLES)
        # Occasionally mutate the invalid example slightly while keeping it
        # human-like (not arbitrary fuzz), to remain deterministic and readable.
        if base and rng.random() < 0.4:
            i = rng.randrange(0, len(base))
            # Flip case of one character if alphabetic, else insert a char.
            ch = base[i]
            if ch.isalpha():
                ch = ch.lower() if ch.isupper() else ch.upper()
                base = base[:i] + ch + base[i+1:]
            else:
                base = base[:i] + "_" + base[i:]
        # Add optional whitespace noise
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pre, suf = rng.choice(SURROUNDS)
            base = f"{pre}{base}{suf}"
        s = base

    # Ensure total length within 4096 bytes (always true here, but keep safe)
    b = s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')[:4096]
    return b
